That combination means structure carries far more information than attributes alone, so the strongest views are the ones that read structure against attributes rather than either in isolation. attr_struct_mismatch leads: it has the widest and best separated upper tail of all landmarkers (std 0.2454, p50 0.3138 rising to p90 0.7175 and p99 0.9141, roughly 2.9x the median), exactly the cross-modal divergence expected when a node's attributes and its position disagree. homophily_violation is the second view and is well licensed by homophily 0.7823: with neighborhoods that agreeable, a mismatch is informative, and its distribution confirms it (p50 0.3628, p95 0.7207, p99 0.8410). It is preferred over local_affinity, which measures the same neighbor-agreement axis with a weaker tail (p99 0.6969) and would be redundant. community adds an independent purely structural view justified by modularity 0.5085 and 50 communities, and its landmarker separates cleanly (p50 0.2295 to p99 0.7341, std 0.1927). conformity supplies the complementary in-lier direction: feature_dup_rate 0.489 clears the template-dominated threshold, so camouflage by conformity is a real mechanism here, and its negative-residual signal is orthogonal to the three mismatch/structure views rather than duplicating them. homophily=0.7823 means most nodes strongly agree with their neighbors, so the local_affinity landmarker's sharp upper tail (p50=0.198 vs p99=0.697, ~3.6 std above median) marks a genuine low-agreement minority worth flagging. The contrastive probe is near-degenerate at the bulk (p50=0.0007, p90=0.0049) but spikes at p99=0.152 (~4 std separation), indicating a small set of nodes with real cross-view disagreement in embedding space, a mechanism orthogonal to raw feature-neighbor comparison and thus complementary. attr_struct_mismatch shows the widest relative spread (std=0.2454 on mean=0.3521, CV=0.70) with p90=0.7175 far above p50=0.3138, consistent with feature_dim=10 and clustering_coeff=0.5329 both being informative but sometimes disagreeing signals, exactly what this cross-modal rank-divergence paradigm targets. spectral adds a genuinely different (frequency-domain) view of structure with its own strong separation (p50=0.1077 to p99=0.5512, ~3.5 std), useful given spectral_gap=0.132 is low enough that community/modularity alone (num_communities=50, modularity=0.5085) may not capture all structural irregularity. density was excluded as degenerate (p50=p90=p95=0, an artifact of avg_degree=88.28 flattening local density), conformity despite feature_dup_rate=0.489 triggering applicability shows a ceiling effect (p50=0.8696 close to p90=0.9357, low relative separation) so it lacks a discriminative tail here, and community/homophily_violation/reconstruction were dropped as redundant with or weaker than the four selected complementary views.

High homophily (0.782) makes local_affinity a clean signal: neighbor-agreement violations stand out against a strongly homophilous baseline, and its landmarker shows the sharpest upper-tail separation of any neighbor-based score (p50 0.198 -> p99 0.697, ~3.4 std above mean). attr_struct_mismatch is independently well-supported (feature_dim=10 satisfies the criterion) and shows the cleanest, most extreme separation in the whole distribution set (p50 0.314 -> p90 0.717 -> p99 0.914), giving a genuinely complementary cross-modal view rather than another neighbor-similarity check. community is backed by real structure (modularity 0.5085, 50 communities) and its landmarker spreads meaningfully (p50 0.230 -> p99 0.734), adding a mesoscale view orthogonal to local/attribute mismatch. spectral rounds out the set with a frequency-domain structural signal that also separates well (p50 0.108 -> p99 0.551, ~3.2 std), useful given the heavy-tailed degree distribution (avg 88.3, std 161.8, max 2138) that high-frequency responses can pick up. Excluded: density's landmarker is degenerate (p50/p90/p95 = 0), consistent with hub-driven degree heterogeneity confounding embedding-space density; homophily_violation is dropped as redundant with local_affinity (same neighbor-mismatch mechanism); conformity, despite meeting the dup_rate>=0.4 criterion, has a compressed near-ceiling landmarker (mean 0.811, p50 0.870) showing most nodes already score high, so it can't isolate a distinct anomalous subset; reconstruction/adversarial/one_class/contrastive probes are weak or degenerate (z-separation low or signal concentrated at floor) and further undermined by low feature_dim (10) and high feature_dup_rate (0.489), which limit how informative raw-feature reconstruction residuals can be.

attr_struct_mismatch has the cleanest separated tail (mean 0.352, p50 0.314, p99 0.914, ~2.6x spread) and is well-motivated here: feature_dim=10 is thin relative to the rich structure (50 communities, modularity 0.5085), so attribute-based and structure-based rankings can genuinely diverge. homophily=0.7823 is high, meaning most nodes agree strongly with neighbors, which makes homophily_violation a sharp, rare signal (p99=0.841 vs p50=0.363, 2.3x spread) for the few nodes that mismatch their neighborhood. community adherence is directly supported by strong modularity (0.5085) and clear community partitioning (50 communities, clustering_coeff=0.5329), with a well-separated score tail (p99=0.734 vs p50=0.230). conformity is explicitly triggered by the high feature_dup_rate (0.489, half the graph shares near-duplicate template feature vectors) — a camouflage-by-conformity mechanism where anomalies hide as feature-space in-liers; its scores sit near ceiling (p50=0.870, p99=0.969), consistent with a templated feature matrix. These four are complementary: two structural (community fit, neighbor homophily), one cross-modal (attribute vs structure), and one feature-space camouflage signal, avoiding redundancy with local_affinity (overlaps with homophily_violation) and embedding-distance paradigms (density's landmark distribution is degenerate — p50=p90=p95=0 — indicating a collapsed embedding space that would also undermine one_class and contrastive).
